chapter: George Lewis and the house bands
title: Hiring George Lewis and hearing him first
summary: Bands were rotated; Papa Celestin's last steady job was here. Sid first heard George Lewis on records and at the Patek Lounge, then hired him twice for months.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Well, can you tell me about how it was that you decided to hire George Lewis, the George Lewis band, and the circumstances, anything you can remember to hire him? George Lewis, yes.

There were a number of good bands around town, of which George had one. And our policy was not to keep the same band for much too long. We would change bands and alternate bands. Paul Baldwin would work a while. By a while, I mean some months. George would come in with his band, and this actually is the last spot that Papa Celestan worked a steady engagement. Two weeks after he left here is when I think he was stricken fatally and died. This is his last steady job right here, Papa Celestan. George was here at two different times, and it was a happy occasion. People thronged in the sea, and they just loved him. They were particularly fond of George, all over the world.
So, where did you, how was it that you had heard George play? Where did you heard him play before getting in here?

Records, first I heard him records. And then the Patek Lounge, which is on the other end of the block, they would bring in bands occasionally. They'd have a house band, and on the off night they would bring in a different band, another band. I guess the first time I heard George Lewis play in person was at the Patek Lounge. And I was impressed. What would be a clarinet player myself of some sort? I was impressed by his style and by his ideas and his technique. George got over the clarinet and put it on good. He was a sweetheart, he was a sweetheart. So when the opportunity presented itself, he did some off nights for us here. And then when it was time to change the band, we put George to work. And as I said, he worked two different occasions for us. Both of them were very happy occasions, incidentally.
Can you remember how long the engagements were?
George, no, I can't recall offhand, of course the contract's in the back, but I think George did about a six month stint at one time and probably another six or eight months at another time.
